# `iscope_get_app_state`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Return the device's function tree: the state of every view, stack, plan and calibration function.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (full command-socket call; shared diagnostic writes; 64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xb5d70 (64-bit build), PrintFuncTree @0x6e2150 |

No params are read. The result is an object keyed by function name; each value is a function node with a state and callback-specific members. A failed function appears as a node with state fail inside a successful outer reply (outer code 0). The name suggests a pure query but printing a completed ViewPlan can save plan state to storage (once), and printing a stack node can close its cached output-file object, hence tier C. The grade reflects the whole request/reply path, which reaches the shared diagnostic logger; it does not by itself mean the method changes device settings.

Side effects: Holds the function-tree mutex while printing; may invoke the completed-plan callback, which sets a saved flag and writes the plan file; may close the cached stack output-file object; main process waits up to 10000 ms for the second camera's state. Every call also performs shared request/reply diagnostic logging.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"iscope_get_app_state"`. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (iscope_get_app_state reply (success)) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | object | yes | - | (iscope_get_app_state reply (success)) Object assembled from the function tree: one member per printable function, keyed by its runtime name (View, SecondView, DarkLibrary, CreateHPC, ViewPlan, Demonstrate and others are expected by the app; none is guaranteed), plus selected_cam on the main process. Ignored nodes are omitted. On the main process the second camera's result members are appended unreconciled when its request succeeds; a failed or unmatched slave request just omits them. The member inventory is open. [READ] |
| `result.selected_cam` | string | no | - | (iscope_get_app_state reply (success)) Main process only: the selected camera, View or SecondView; unknown if the lookup fails. One of: `View`, `SecondView`, `unknown`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (iscope_get_app_state reply (success)) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (iscope_get_app_state reply (success)) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

No handler-specific error is reachable. Plan-save and slave-query failures do not become error replies. Nested node failures carry their own code and error inside the result.

## Example

Request, poll - Bare request; the iOS app sends this after connecting (OBSERVED, 2026-10-12):

```json
{"id":51,"method":"iscope_get_app_state"}
```

Reply, ok - Shape only; node names, members and values are invented:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"iscope_get_app_state","result":{"View":{"state":"working","lapse_ms":120000,"stage":"Stack","mode":"star","cam_id":0,"lp_filter":false,"gain":80},"Stack":{"state":"working","lapse_ms":118000,"stacked_frame":12,"dropped_frame":1,"can_annotate":false,"scene_shooting":false,"frame_errcode":0},"selected_cam":"View"},"code":0,"id":51}
```
